PROS:
1. GREAT GAMEPLAY - If you liked Borderlands 2, you will like this game. The movement, the guns, and the environments are awesome. The gameplay is so good it almost makes up for the shortcomings, of which there are many. Seriously, the gunplay is absolutely fantastic!
2. Loot - Once again, guns are fantastic. I always loved finding new guns/shields/relics/etc.
3. Bosses - I really liked how each boss felt different and most had interesting mechanics to go along with them, however there is also a CON here that I will get into later.
4. Skills - I played through the game as Zane, and the amount of customization to the skills and abilities is AMAZING! This is easily the most fleshed out skill system in the series and really made me feel that every point mattered.

CONS:
1. Bosses - SO MANY IMMUNITY STAGES! Seriously, who thought that was a good idea? Almost half the bosses have "stages" where they sit there and charge up or whatever, and are immune to damage for sometimes up to a full minute in the middle of the battle! Very annoying and really breaks the fast paced boss fights.
2. Characters - In Borderlands 2, the characters were the absolutely best thing about the game! So many memorable people, lines, and moments. In this game there are so few that only one comes to mind while writing this review. No Mr. Torgue(Well, other than a slaughter mini-game), Lilith is a waste in this game, Mordecai/Brick are almost nonexistent, no Axton, Gaige, Krieg(Other than his voice), or Salvador, Maya is relegated to a plot point, and for some reason Hammerlock is now a whiny baby and not a fearless explorer. If you are looking for another amazing villain like Handsome Jack, prepare to be disappointed. And that leads us into point 3...
3. Ava - I don't even know what to say about this character. She is the "Typical obnoxious teenager who never does what she's told and always does stupid things that literally get people killed but never accepts responsibility for her actions" character and yet she STILL GETS REWARDED for being a useless dolt. Her dialogue is so bad I just started turning down my speakers every time she opened her mouth. Half her lines are yelling at characters and inanimate objects. Just an abysmal character and since she plays such an important part in the story it stands out the most out of all the poor choices for this story.
4. The Story - (I will be as vague as possible to avoid spoilers) Honestly, it's not that bad, until they seemed to abandon the plot they had been foreshadowing. The main villains are incredibly annoying, but then things start to change just before the halfway point of the game and they actually become a little interesting! There is conflict and it seemed like the story was going to take a really interesting direction, and then they abandoned it. The last third of the game is a bit of a slog but it would have been better had they gone a different route for the final boss. Overall, mediocre villains at best, and other than Promethea the planet stories were kinda boring or useless. 

Overall - I recommend this game for the gameplay and loot, which is the core of any looter-shooter, but it was really disappointing to not get another good story. By the end of Borderlands 2, I felt very attached the characters and I wanted to kill Handsome Jack so badly I stayed up late at night just to beat the game! I honestly don't even feel like I want to go back through the story again, except for Promethea. I got it on sale at 50% off, which I would definitely recommend. This is not a game I would pay full price for. It may seem like I am really ragging on the game, which is fair, but I also think it had a ton to live up to after the fantastic game that was Borderlands 2. When dialogue comes up, I role my eyes and shake my head, but the rest of the time I'm sliding, mantling, slamming, shooting, and stabbing my way through hordes of enemies, which is so much fun I forget about the bad stuff!

If you don't give a sh*t about story and just wanna shoot stuff, this game is 10/10.

If you care about the story, this game is 4/10. If Ava was killable I'd give it 8/10.

I actively play this game with my father who enjoys shotguns. The creativity of the different shotguns he can experience and the feel of the weapon have lead him to this summary review: "pretty good game for 20 bucks" which is a level above his satisfactory review of: "it's okay" when it comes to reviewing entertainment of any kind (games, movies, TV).

In terms of my personal point-of-view, I deeply enjoy the perpetual escort mission that is leading my father to where the danger is and routinely reviving him because he has not figured out how to move and shoot simultaneously. To add, the ability to ping the map to call for him like a dog has immensely improved my the efficiency of my communication skills while also helping him see key items and weapons for him to consider (he suffers from progressive ophthalmoplegia).

Lastly, I would rate this game as "fairly difficult" due to the necessity of needing to constantly revive him throughout fights, thus massively increasing the longevity and engagement with this game.

In conclusion, I would rate this game fairly enjoyable in spending time with my father who is nearing retirement, learning how to play video games and seldom physically visit due to COVID and our geo. locations (US to EU).

I waited for the Steam release, so this is a fresh take. With about 100 hours in BL1 and 700 in BL2, I think this one falls somewhere between the two in terms of quality.
+The guns are the best in the franchise--each feeling unique and worth experimenting with. I actually find some early game greens and blues INTERESTING to use, where once I was solely condemned to using them until I could afford a DPUH & Grog. Rarity also seems to have been given a boost; not only do legendaries drop at a more generous rate, but purples are also noticeably better than common stock, where they used to inspire the thought, 'aww, why didn't RNG just give me an orange instead?'
+Vehicles are fun and not quite as finicky as the previous entries.
+All four characters seem worth playing and potentially viable late-game.
-Matchmaking needs a tuneup before it can even be compared to the perfection of BL2 in that respect.
-The bias towards co-op (at least in the early game) is very noticeable. Little effort was given to balance the experience of a solo player vs the experience of a four-person squad.
-No offence to the gentleman who took over voice acting Claptrap--but it just ain't the same. Gearbox's magician sure knows how to make friends disappear.
-The writing is as weak or weaker than BL1, with many attempts at jokes falling flat and the reprised characters in general coming across as imitations of themselves rather than the real deal. While many lay most of the cringe at the feet of the main villains, I actually find them passable. We were never going to get another Handsome Jack, and the cringy d-baggery they embody is at least intentional and self-aware. All in all, it is clear that gameplay mechanics were given the lion's share of the energy, with the writing as an afterthought. This was BL1's approach, so it's only a letdown in comparison to the awesome balance struck by BL2.
+-Humanoid mobs' movement speeds are greatly increased. For the first time playing the franchise, I had to turn my mouse sensitivity up to consistently land shots.
-Early game, mobs are way more dangerous than bosses.
=Worth the $50 for the whole shebang, and to fans of the franchise will probably merit at least 100 hours. Unfortunately, one doubts it will enjoy the lifespan of BL2, due to the fact that its story and thus replays are not as endearing.

[h1]Borderlands 3 is a good game, ruined by the greed of 2K and Pitchford.[/h1]
I want to preface this review with the fact that I really enjoyed Borderlands 3, FAR MORE than I did with any other Borderlands game. I adored both the shooting and RPG elements of BL3, I think it's the best in the series. I get what I want in Borderlands the most in BL3, fun and insane guns. The close range explosive Flakker, the laser pistol Lightshow, the slot machine integrated gun Lucky 7, and the gun that shoots fucking burgers are all inventions of madmen and I love them. The playable characters are also the best in the series. Multiple action skills allow for you to have 4 BL2 characters in a single BL3 Vault Hunter. There's no real generic gun man (like Axton, Roland, and Wilhelm) and all of them can be played in unique methods. Endgame is also significantly better than BL2's, as Mayhem levels don't require an hour long investment and all of them are free to you in an instant. A final note that a lot of people are sleeping on, you only have to do a single playthrough per character to experience all the content in the game! Honestly dread starting new characters in Borderlands 2, because a max level character entails visiting Sawtooth Cauldron 3 times.

Now why is this review negative? Let's start off with the apparent reasons that are actually in the game. The UI is nauseating, the mini-maps are an actual challenge to navigate due to how they factor in different floor levels and how they constantly rotate. The same mini-map will look drastically different from itself if you just move up a staircase and face the other way. Also, it is not my expertise to say why, but BL3 has terrible optimization and even the highest end pcs will experience stutters over very little. But the most offending factor of BL3 would be the game's writing. The main story has some of the worst writing I've seen in a AAA game. Ava is probably one of my least favorite characters from this decade. She is a literal child that constantly whines and learns nothing, but for some reason gets the keys to the Crimson Raiders thrown her way. And don't even get me started on the Calypso twins. Living up to Handsome Jack is a very difficult task, but they were miles away from ever achieving that. Tyreen's motivations are the generic "I want power for the sake of it" villain trope and Troy exists for a buildup to nothing. If you want a more detailed explanation on the faults of BL3's story, I highly recommend Cartoonshi's video on the topic.

What I care most about however is the numerous shoddy business practices of 2K and Randy Pitchford. BL3 is a $60 game with another $80 worth of DLC in its 2 season passes. The $115 asking price for all the game's content is baffling to me and I cannot justify that cost for any video game. Not to mention the fact that a second season pass betrays the promise that season pass holders get all future DLC content. Oh and there was also the Epic Games Exclusive deal. A complete lack of care for their consumers by locking the game behind an inferior storefront. The money from said deal didn't even go to the developers, but rather the greedy executives as Gearbox devs never received their promised bonuses after the game sold 5 million copies. This combined with the allegations of assault and severe underpay from the former Claptrap voice actor really lead me to believe that Gearbox is a talented studio held back by their money-grubbing publishers. I genuinely hope Gearbox will be able to stand without 2K someday.

As a TLDR: I love BL3, it's a very fun game with some flaws in UI, optimization, and writing. But I find the toxic work environment of 2K, underpaying of employees, and the anti-consumer business practices make it very hard for me to recommend anyone to get it. 2K is a company up there with EA with their abuse and greed and I hope that less people support them.

Borderlands 3 is a first-person looter shooter game, and represents the fourth main and fifth overall entry in Gearbox Software's Borderlands game series.

[i] Pros & cons: [/i]

++ More guns, more enemies, more Borderlands! The core gunplay mechanics have been improved, especially in regards of weapon design and build diversity. And remember, if it took more than one shot, you weren't using a Jakobs.

+ Visit the inhabitants of other planets, and blow them up. The different worlds you can visit add some fresh breath into the adventurous life of a vault hunter. It feels like a Schnitzeljagd on a galactic scale.

+ The various addons provide additional, high quality content. My favourite one is Guns, Love, and Tentacles; it has a solid lovecraftian foundation with a bit of a twist.

o On the one hand, I am happy to see that most of the side characters from the previous instalments have been included into this game. On the other hand, they are criminally underused, and a certain teenage girl, for her unholy name shall not be mentioned, should have never made it... *looks at the Interplanetary Ninja Assassin Claptrap* I have a job for you.

o The drop rate of unique items is ridiculously high. Actually, I have amassed such a quantity of them, all the bling-bling on me blinds my enemies. In addition, a rap label has offered me a recording contract.

- The concept of several immunity stages during boss encounters does not belong in a looter shooter, because it breaks the fluidity of combat, and diminishes the level of difficulty. If not for this mechanism, I would have melted the face of the final boss within five seconds! 

-- I do not know what tragedy must have happened in the storyboard room, and at this point I am too afraid to ask. But, the amateurish execution and presentation of the narrative in combination with the insufferable depiction of both main villains speak for excessive drug abuse and / or an overdose of social media.

[i] Summary: [/i]

Borderlands 3 is worthy successor to one of the greatest shooters ever made, and I like that it remains true to its core gameplay in form of shoot it & let the loot rain from the heavens. 
Alas, I consider the main storyline a train wreck, and the attempt of a social parody a failed experiment.

Recommended for gun geeks and gamers with a hoarding disorder.

I have nearly 600 hours in this game and I would not recommend it to others. I've thought about reviewing it several times but I haven't until now because it's impossible to do so without blasting it for its' bad points, and I feel bad for doing that because it does have some really good points as well. 

[h1] + THE GOOD + [/h1] 
[list]
 [*]The combat mechanics are excellent, and the gunplay specifically is f__king phenomenal. Huge variety, procedurally generated, cool legendaries. Maybe the best gunplay I've seen in a game. 
 [*]There are some interesting character build options with synergies between skills, gear etc. Again no complaints with the mechanical side of things. 
 [*]There are, to be fair, a few good characters. Mr Torgue is great. Mancubus, Maurice and Pain/Terror are at least pretty good. 
 [*]Most of the voice acting is very good. In fact it's generally excellent, just let down by the writing. 
 [*]There's a pretty good variety of enemies. 
 [*]Mayhem mode is a great idea and it's well implemented.
 [*]The Guns, Love and Tentacles DLC is pretty good in its' entirety. Much closer to BL2 than the rest of the game.
[/list]

[h1] + THE WRITING + [/h1] 
[list]
 [*]I feel bad for how harsh this is going to be but many aspects of the writing; particularly the story but also other stuff, are the worst I've seen in a game. It's banal, it's trite, it's lame and stupid and overly aggrandising... it's the special kind of bad that needs its' own section just to cover everything. 
 [*]Borderlands has always been a bit kitsch but BL3 is almost nothing but, and constant in-your-face kitsch is, of course, obnoxious AF. How did nobody at Gearbox see that? Plus because it's deliberately kitsch it almost gives the impression the game was badly written on purpose. That's an achievement.
 [*]Most characters seem to be on the spectrum for some reason (I support equality but seriously 60% of people don't have ASDs in real life) while others are just pieces of wood. The mission dialogues usually consist of the spectrum circus doing brainfarts for several minutes then the piece of wood does the thing to move the story along, which is usually a line that could be replaced with "I'm sorry Mario, but the Princess is in another castle." It's a good thing the Eridians split the vault keys into pieces because otherwise they'd be real short on missions. 
 [*]Half the characters feel the need to constantly tell you how f__king awesome and important you are, and how much everyone needs you. A spaceship full of sycophants. That's fun. 
 [*]Occasionally you'll hear a line of dialogue that was so badly written you can tell the voice actor couldn't even work out what they were supposed to be saying. 
 [*]I laughed at two jokes the entire game. 
[/list]

[h1] + THE REST OF THE BAD + [/h1] 
[list]
 [*]After giving people the option to buy the "season pass" on release, they have released a second "season pass" with not much content and a few OP weapons so players feel like they need to buy it to have the best gear. I can respect the hustle of a shiny turd salesman, but they're still selling turds. 
 [*]The 4 DLCs that were part of season pass 1 followed a similar path. DLC 3 and 4 were increasingly rushed and of poor quality, with DLC 4 released in under 3 months from DLC 3. No wonder it was such a trashfire. Then again they never stipulated whether the season pass DLCs you'd get would be any good, just that you'd get 4 of them. Then 2K can get Gearbox to turn out a fifth trash DLC 2.5 months later so they can start charging people who had already paid for the game and the season pass. So that's what they did. Probably not a practice we should be supporting. 
 [*]There are a lot of boring fetch quests. There are a few good ones as well but they're few and far between. 
 [*]The music is bad, except for the Revenge of the Cartels special event. That's only available for one month of the year though. 
 [*]The atmosphere / world building is pretty absent. Planets feel like stages rather than worlds to be explored. 
 [*]The AI is below par even for a game you don't expect to have good AI. 
[/list]

So basically the gunplay is the best thing ever, the writing is the worst thing ever, and 2K likes to rip their customers off as much as they can get away with. If you could get the full game (aka the "Ultimate Edition") for about $40US then I would say do it, but otherwise it's just too much money for a game with so many bad points.

Borderlands 3 is the fourth game in the Borderlands series, and as such it should be excellent, benefiting from the combined experience of a team that's made and polished essentially the exact same game four times. In one respect, the visuals, it is. But in every other, notably story and gameplay, Borderlands 3 either makes no improvements on its predecessors or outright fails to live up to them.

The story of Borderlands 3 is easily summarized: a brand-new group of Vault Hunters need to stop some evil twins from ending the universe. Unfortunately, this never happens. The player characters never, ever interact with any story character in any cutscene throughout the entire game. While you're playing you can talk to story characters and take missions from them, but the second anything of import happens the Vault Hunters disappear and the story characters walk in, leaving the player feeling like they aren't even involved in the story.

As for that story... It doesn't know what it is. The antagonists (refered to as the Twins from here on out) are played completely straight, even though elements of their backstory are totally ridiculous. The Twins want to literally destroy the entire universe. Why? [spoiler]Their dad wasn't a very good dad.[/spoiler] Not abusive, not awful, just 5/10, mediocre. So they want to destroy all life. In previous Borderlands games this would be played as comedy; a motivation this ridiculous would have jokes made about it. Here, in Borderlands 3? This stupidity is treated as deadly serious.

The game goes for explaining the Twins' legion of obsessed followers. No real thought is given to justifying a limitless horde willing to destroy the universe - where they [b]live[/b] - so the answer is handwaved. The Twins are popular streamers and their viewers are willing to die for them. End of story. Again, this wouldn't be a problem in a comedy, but this is treated just as seriously as their motivation.

Further compounding the frustrating aspects of the story is the fact that our protagonists (but not player characters; remember, we never see the player) are all idiots. Not fun idiots, comedic idiots, but frustratingly stupid characters. Our main protagonist, Lilith, can teleport at will, move anywhere. She knows the only thing she has to do is not be within touching distance of the Twins or they will sap her powers. What does she do? You guessed it.

But don't worry. Everyone learned from Lilith, right? No one would do that twice. Enter Maya, a character that can place a bubble around someone and prevent them from acting. She would definitely use that power to subdue one of the Twins rather than, say, [b]put him in a headlock[/b], right? Wrong.

And so on and so forth. The entire plot feels either frustrating or boring, and is interspersed with as many annoying characters as the writers could possibly think of (which is a lot). Sadly, most of the Vault Hunters the player can play as are also boring, but special mention needs to go to Zane. Zane is impeccably voiced by Cian Barry and is, without exaggeration, the only reason I finished the game. His dialogue is hilarious and is so much better written than anything else in Borderlands 3 that I suspect Cian Barry may have improvised it.

But enough about story. You aren't playing a looter shooter for the story! You're here for the gameplay. 

Oops, there's no gameplay.

Or rather, gameplay is this: walk into an area. An NPC yells some dialogue at you and enemies spawn. Kill them until they stop spawning, move to the next area, and repeat. Every zone, all game, no variations, no mechanics. Sure, the guns feel good to shoot, which is nice. There are absurd variations and a huge number of unique guns with unique effects, but all you're doing all game is killing in an arena and moving on. You never have to be reactive to anything, never have to dodge, never have to think. You shoot and aim at the weakspot (if you feel like it). Bosses are exactly same, but usually have one ability that puts a red circle on the ground you need to not stand in. Or you can just stand in it, who cares? Every character has regeneration or leech, so you'll be fine.

But what if you want a challenge? What if you want to fight enemies at 10,000% strength? Well good news: someone at Gearbox played enough Diablo 3 to [b]steal the Torment system directly from that game[/b] and call it Mayhem.

Mayhem works by scaling both enemies and item drops up as you increase Mayhem level, starting at 200% at Mayhem 1 and increasing  to 10,000% at Mayhem 10. In Diablo 3, the game they stole this from, you need to slowly climb in difficulty because your character's damage is all scaled off weapon damage; you need to farm new items with each increase in order to not die. Borderlands 3 scales your shooting damage off weapon damage, but not your Vault Hunter's abilities; these scale with Mayhem level. This means that, for Vault Hunters with pets or long-duration abilities, you can immediately set the game to Mayhem 10 and watch your abilities kill everything with little difficulty.

There's also nothing stopping any Vault Hunter from setting the game to Mayhem 10 and simply running around looking for chests full of guns, hoping to find something good and trying not to die. The entire system is so easily trivialized that I have no idea why it exists; it basically just makes everything a bullet sponge. (And it makes every enemy scream all the time. Things have large enough health bars that ailments you apply to them last a long time, and every mob screams its head off when it has certain ailments. There is no enemy noise adjustment. Get used to it, you'll be hearing it a lot.)

Mayhem is not the only system that seems to exist for no reason. Every character can melee, but it's never used mechanically. Every character can slam by jumping off a high place and crouching, but slam is literally only used once all game: when it's [b]introduced[/b]. There is a post-max-level skill that allows you to slam from a normal jump, making it possible to use it in combat, but that skill takes 100 post-max-level levels. Absurd! You'll never, ever use it, but it exists and could have been used mechanically to add variety and challenge. The same goes for running, sliding, and crouching. All exist, all unused.

There are arena sections in the game, but they don't feel different from normal gameplay because normal gameplay is just arenas already. There is a battle royale mode which is fun once or twice, but it disables your Vault Hunter's abilities, so every run just feels like a generic character shooting, and it has to be balanced around a naked character with no skills and bad guns, so it's pathetically easy.

All told, this lack of synergy between systems and the shallowness of each of them is, sadly, what defines Borderlands 3. The best way to summarize the game is simply that it's just [i]messy[/i]. It feels like it was designed by 5 or 6 different teams who never spoke to each other, and only met for the first time to combine their seperate projects into one huge, jumbled mess of a game.

Borderlands 3 has some of the worst writing I've seen in a modern video game. Clearly suffering from the loss of Anthony Burch, the writer for Borderlands 2 (and the best written entry in the series), Gearbox has fashioned a story so bad that it ruins a game that has seemingly improved in literally every other way.

"The only bad parts are the characters, the story and the way that it's told."
- Paraphrased from Redlettermedia re. the Star Wars prequels

Most of the returning characters are written inconsistently with who they are in the past. Claptrap has lost all the heart, emotion and self-awareness behind his performance and is relegated to just a stupid, mean, egotistical robot.

Lilith worked well as the straight-man comedic character after the departure of Roland to keep a lot of the more eccentric characters grounded - for example, in the Tiny Tina DLC she's the one who chides Tina for eating nothing but crumpets. I feel like she was meant to be a witty, smarmy character on the sidelines who's very powerful, but secretly insecure about her powers and leadership abilities. That is why she defers to Roland's leadership. But in Borderlands 3 we immediately see her as the competent and cock-sure leader of the Crimson Raiders, and it feels out of character to me. That feels like something she should have to earn over the course of this game. As it stands now, in Borderlands 3 she has no character arc, and thus [spoiler] her self sacrifice at the end comes completely out of left field - it feels hollow and unearned. [/spoiler]

And I've held off on talking about the characters everyone knows sucks because... well everyone already knows. The villains are terrible. Nearly every new side character is flat and terrible. Ava actually has a small character arc, and yet she's the most hated of any other new character. If someone told me that one of the new characters in this game is their favorite in the entire franchise, I'd have to ask if they have brain damage - at the very least they know nothing about good character writing.

The celebrity guest cameos, like [spoiler] Ice-T and Penn & Teller [/spoiler], are probably some of the best examples of what's wrong with the writing here. They were unironically some of the most fun sections of the entire game for me. But at the same time they don't factor into the main story at all - they feel like a complete aside. I almost wonder if they hadn't secured those voice actors if those sections would have been included in the game at all. They don't thematically fit into the main storyline at all. Instead they feel like overindulgent side quests that drag out the run time of an already excessively padded game. Forcing them into the main storyline only distracts from the plot of the game, and development time spent on them could have gone into tightening up and revising the script.

And honestly I'm just scratching the surface here. So many characters, side quests, plot lines, and jokes fall flat in this game. The writers completely forgot about the comedic concept of the straight-man, because hundreds of jokes in this game fall flat without the dry sarcasm needed to keep the humor grounded. Instead the vast majority of characters feel like crazy assholes, and I just want someone to pipe in and say, "Shut up you insane fools."

And frankly at this point that's exactly what I want someone to say to their writing staff.

Oh and I guess I should mention: the new movement systems are a blast, interactions feel more weighty and satistfying, the new guns are fun (except for Maliwan which feel horrible), the planets and scenery are beautiful, the sound and music is great. I swear this is the Game of Thrones of video games - the great works of hundreds of talented people ruined by bad writing.

Preface: As I near the end of the game I'm very, very close to switching my opinion. As it stands, with the full $60 price tag, I'll warn you that you're getting fantastic gunplay- and nothing else.



[strike]I'd still recommend for the $30 sale[/strike] and the vastly improved gunplay and abilities. But (and it's a long list of buts) the humor isn't there; often flat or annoying. The returning cast of characters is small and bland and the new ones unremarkable. The menus are beyond annoying. Parts of BL3 are tiring they're so dull. It's only the slick gunplay and environments  that are keeping me compelled. Exploration will now reward you with hidden and challenging fights, or pieces of a map leading to treasure. Mantling is a new mechanic that introduces platforming to ledges and surfaces a la Mirror's Edge in order to find loot. And there are a lot of loot containers. Too much, as most are just small ammo caches. And, my favorite weapon type, sniper rifles just kind of...suck. (My gameplay has relied on an early pistol I found that reads "500% Crit Damage" which has created a really fun loop of 1-hit kills as long as I can land a critical hit. My other weapons supplement the pistol's low raw-damage. That goes to show that weapon versatility can still have a significant impact on gameplay if you choose to pursue it.)

The character I chose, Zane, has a playstyle of run-and-gun. Literally. He gets bonuses from moving while shooting. And the option to equip one of three skills (or two if you're willing to sacrifice the ability to use grenades) makes combat much more dynamic with more options than previous entries (I have a damage-amplifying shield to put down when things get too chaotic and a flying turret to help finish off kills all while never stopping to stand still). Gun-specific skill trees are gone, however, as are gun-specific skills which I was sad about because I liked being challenged to find a gun type and stick with it for its specific bonuses.

While the complaints from other reviews are beyond valid, one thing I don't see people talk about is the abysmal UX. The HUD is fine- no complaints. It's bright, poppy, and I never felt that I didn't know what was going on in combat. But navigating menus is a trainwreck. Visually they're so cluttered, so compact, that it's hard to read and absorb any information. Navigation never feels easy, only clunky. The feats/challenges from BL2 are back- the ones that would give you challenge points to spend on tiny stat upgrades but as far as I can tell there aren't any points to spend. I say that without confidence because even the navigation to see these challenges is absurd, and they pop up as notifications for finishing/almost finishing X task so it's not like they're easy to ignore. To see your progress you no longer navigate to a tab in the menu. Instead, you open the map, press X once to switch from local view to planet view, then X again to switch from planet to galaxy view, then select the challenges tab where the categorization and grouping of the skills are terrible. And you're never told this. It's so unintuitive that I imagine most players find it by accident or through several minutes of trial and error. Navigating back to check progress is a pain.

But the absolute worst thing is the inability to look at multiple quests on your map. To see where your objective is on the map you open the menu/press M. But if you want to see the locations of any other objectives you must either close the menu and use the hotkeys to switch quests, or navigate to the Quests tab and select a different quest then return to the map. And looking at the description of a quest no longer tells you what area the quest is located in. Think of how many sidequests there are in Borderlands and how you look at the map to plan the most efficient route to tackle them all in. Well, no longer. 

The gameplay has been significantly improved and expanded. New enemies and new enemy types, new attacks, new gun behaviors, new abilities (three unique ones per character), new mantling, new sliding, new vehicle parts, new skill trees offering 2 or 3 different playstyles per character- the gameplay feels like a proper sequel. It feels fresh and rejuvenated. But navigating the UI is painful. And dear god is the story dull. The writing is flat; it's jokes lazy, forced, or outdated. It's that exhausting kind of dull, like it's not even worth the energy to explain how empty it is. Most of all- it's just not charming. So Borderlands 3 will forever be one of those "exception" games, one with an asterisk. The kind a friend would recommend heartily but with a "as long as you ignore..."

EDIT: The cast of returning characters does grow considerably larger, but not until ~20 hrs in. There are far, far fewer sidequests (2-3 per area). You also can't see how much XP is left until you level up (the specific number you have vs how much is needed. You can still see the amount of XP you receive from each kill, but without being able to see the sum it might as well just be a slowly filling yellow bar).

Borderlands 3 has many facets that are great, and clear upgrades to its predecessors, such as the satisfying gunplay and the improved visuals. The game can be incredibly fun when you just get to zoom around the gameworld, shooting and killing everything that has a healthbar. The new vault hunters - Fl4k, Moze, Amara and Zane - have much more intricate and varied skill trees, and the introduction of Mayhem Mode should - in theory - add some much needed endgame. Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode (UVHM) was thankfully removed, and we don't have to deal with slag as a necessary evil anymore, either.
Bossfights are generally decent. They aren't particularly mechanical or demanding, but get the job done.
Co-op is (as always) the best aspect of the game, it can truly be a blast.

However, moments when the game is purely enjoyable are rare.
The first and most obvious weakness is the writing of the game. Characters are tropey, to the point that they feel like their dialogue was generated by a GenZ intern using ChatGPT. While the terrible dialogue adequately lends itself to the very one-dimensional villains, which are essentially just evil for evils sake and lack the same depth that Handsome Jack had in BL2, it becomes increasingly unbearable as the game goes on.
Don't even get me started on Ava, who might just be the worst character in any video game series so far.
There seems to be one repeating plot device: You defeat some kind of minor villain, you enter a fairly uninteresting, small vault for a minute, shit happens once you come out (someone gets killed or kidnapped, generally) and then you have to resolve the occurred shit before you can enter the next vault.

The pacing is pretty awful, as well. During the story (or any sidequest for that matter) you will also have to just sit around, waiting for dialogue to end, -constantly-. Buttons will be locked before a character has finished their speech, and the same holds true for objects that can only be destroyed once you have sat around long enough. This is fine on the first playthrough, but takes away massively from the replayability of the game. I'll illustrate my annoyance with one particular pair of scenes from about three-quarters through the game. As part of the previous planet, you picked up the mentor-figure (Maya) and a tagalong kid (Ava). On the current planet, in the vault you open, the kid (despite everyone telling her to stay put) sneaks in (somehow, despite all the monsters). Because of this, Maya hangs back to watch her while you go into the vault. When you come out, cutscene-incompetence engages and you, Maya, and the kid all stand around gormlessly while the villains drain the vault guardian's power. The kid stupidly yells about how Maya is going to beat them up, causing a distraction which allows one of the villains to drain the power/life from Maya. Despite the obvious fear this should cause in the kid, she continues taunting them until the villain force-pushes her across the room and they flee.

Back on the ship, everyone is having a sad remembrance of the fallen mentor (at least I think it was sad; I was just bored). The kid gets angry at the messiah-figure (Lilith), yelling that Lilith was at fault for Maya's death because Lilith allowed her to go on that mission. Not a single person corrects the kid, or consoles Lilith. Everyone acts as if the kid has just spouted the truth. *facepalm*

After that cutscene, I did some digging and discovered the cause of this stupidity: BL3 has 4 writers. Only one of them has any writing experience prior to this (another bad game) and only one has any significant experience... in visual effects. Was Gearbox so strapped for cash that they literally couldn't hire a single writer with any skill? Did they care so little about anything in this game that they thought hiring 4 no-names was a good idea? There are so many starving writers out there with the right chops for worldbuilding, but apparently Gearbox hates anything that isn't guns. Rather fitting, that.

[h1] [b] BORDERLINE A BORDERLANDS [/b] [/h1]

[i] This review is by someone (me) who has played all Borderlands games, and enjoyed them.
It will not (bar this) mention the anti-consumer exclusive practices used before launch, nore will it be affected by other ‘events’, this is a review of the game (weirdly). Now that's dealt with. [/i]


[b]Borderlands 3 had some pretty big shoes to fill with the success of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Fifth_Quarter/recommended/49520]Borderlands 2[/url], but did it?[/b]

🔸 [b] Main Story [/b]
It’s pretty shocking, especially compared with BL2.
The antagonists are annoying, shallow and offer nothing more than an eventual target.
It answers some of the questions from as early as BL1 but it seems too forced and leaves you with more questions (as if this is a BL2.5)
In all it's a device to get you to other planets to shoot things, a far cry from the mystery and double faced Handsome Jack.
BL3 also echoes (almost direct copy’s) major plot points in BL2.
Although they are far weaker in presentation and execution.
By the end of my first playthrough I wanted it to just end, where as I love playing BL2 even now (2500h+ later) as if it's the first time, listening to NPC’s, exploring maps and playing side missions, BL3 doesn't do that for me, I can’t pinpoint it but it's boring, this ‘Mayhem’ never surfaces, and I never thought i'd say this for a Borderlands game, [b] the shooting gets Old [/b]

🔹 [b] Side Quests [/b]
This helped make BL2 as big and in depth as it was and BL3 has a similar approach, but as with the main story they eventually become nothing more than waypoint following exercises (yes basically they all are), but they too have lost the magic and appeal from BL2.

🔸 [b] Environments [/b]
This is on a similar level with BL2, some fimillier places and plenty of new ones with their own unique styles & enemies.
They have focused more on larger areas (more tech advancements) although it does feel like there is considerably less here than BL2, great areas of nothing and noone.

🔹 [b] Vault Hunters [/b]
They are not bad, but neither are they the best.
A lot of the perks are do A & B to get reward, opposed to a permanent increase in a stat, so by the time you're a high/max level you are juggling several of these every engagement, it feels more like a management sim than a shooter here.
Although I love the ability to have multiple action skills that can be affected/augmented in different ways, this would give great repeatability (if the rest was overall worth it)

🔸 [b] Guns [/b]
Weapon manufacturers still (I believe for the better) have specific characteristics, although they have been tweaked and added too (A big plus).
This make all manufacturers viable throughout the game (something that needed to be addressed following BL2)
However some of the firing styles (looking at Maliwan and Atlas) can be off putting, this then effectively removes them from some players' viable weapon list.

E-Tech has been reworked and butchered IMO (they now have an Alien melted barrel)
They no longer fire type specific ammo.
This is a big let down for a lot of fans as we were hoping that the progression of E-tech would lead to all guns being able to fire all types (eg: shotgun firing pistol needles or assault rifle firing sniper beams) but no.

Slag is gone, Cryo from BL1.5 has been added and a new Radiation type has been created.
Lasers (BL1.5) have not made an appearance as a weapon type but some weapons do fire similar effects (Malliwan)

It’s not that I think BL2 guns were bad but BL3 guns are gorgeous and they sound hefty, as if you're firing huge rounds instead of the tinny ting from BL2 Maliwan’s for example.

🔹 [b] Other Gear [/b]
Class mods are pretty much as BL2 with more variation,
Grenades are similar but can now have more variation of BL2,
Relics have been revamped (mostly to fit new skills/ playstyle option)
Shields have had a similar rework,

🔸 [b] Vehicles [/b]
Vehicles were never a massive thing in Borderlands, they had their moments, a few quests that you needed them for, a race here n there.
BL3 now allows for part customisation, Great, at least on the surface.
Other than getting you around these upgraded/personalised death machines are not used ANYWHERE (bar mission specific vehicles you are given for the duration!)
A race league where specific parts where needed would have been great, but NO, this additional and heavily advertised element adds nothing substantial to the game and one of many things that feel like it has been cut short.

🔹 [b] Loot Mechanics [/b]
This has been tweaked and is a double edged sword.
When you start a game you can can pick between the original loot system and divy it up between you and your partners or the new individual loot pools that prevent loot ninjas and hoarders hovering up everything and complaining that you and your white starter pistol can’t take on a lvl 20 Badass!

In reality the amount of Legendaries the game throws at you nigates the above & diminishes their value.
⚠️ Worse, this breaks the loot tier system making almost everything below useless and destroys the loot mechanics the franchise is identified by/relies on. ⚠️

🔸 [b] Game Play [/b]
This is upped from BL2, mostly thanks to more modern mechanics and addition of little features like sliding. (Although the fact you can slide up Stairs is just, wrong)
No surprise here as BL2 was/is not lacking in this department.

🔹 [b] Dialog [/b]
It’s bad, most of it feels like filler and with little to none of the feeling of BL2.
And the jokes, what jokes, BL1, 2, Tales & even 1.5 had better humour in general, but that’s OK, that’s not like it's always been a big part of the franchise...

🔸 [b] History [/b]
In previous Borderlands we have either through conversations, missions or Echos learned about current or past Vault hunters and others around the story and events that have/are/will happen.
There is so little of that here.
Yes we see a few of the original vault hunters & a handful of others from BL2. [b] THAT'S IT [/b]
No mentions of Salvador, Axton, Gaige (until DLC), Krieg or Athena who was at the very end of the BL2 timeline, she just vanishes.
Then you have Scooter, He gets so little mention,I know Tales went over it, but a mural on Sanctuary 3 is all.
It’s these kinds of things that BL2 would have had a little something on that would help build the world. BL3 lacks this and as such makes it just a shooter.

🔹 [b] Other [/b]
Quality of life improvements have been added throughout and give it a nice up from its predecessor.
They have introduced an ‘Easy mode’ although I can't’ comment on as I can’t see me ever using it, and to be honest the ‘Normal’ (hardest) difficulty is easy, BL2 gave me a run for my money BL3 no challenge, which brings me on to…,
⚠️ Bosses, with [b]Forced Invincibility[/b] periods that ruin the flow of the fight.
⚠️ The amount of long, bad, unskippable dialog stopping you from doing anything else.
⚠️ Inventory still glitches, despite several patch notes stating otherwise (now 1 year on)
⚠️ Co-Op is [b] STILL [/b] (for a lot), a lag fest and unplayable if you can connect at all.


🔸 [b] Summery [/b]
Borderlands 3 is a good game, it plays well, looks good (not too sure on Lilith’s remodel), the rebalanced manufactures work (ish), more gun options and quality of life improvements are always a plus.

Yet as a Borderlands game, despite all the community comments/feedback/ideas following BL1, 1.5, 2, & the hype from the publishers, BL3 is more like a generic shooter.

They can/have done far better and that hurts this title a lot.

You can't follow a masterpiece like Borderlands 2 with some knockoff cover that's missing half the cast, gets nowhere with the story slowly, explains little to why we're doing things & kills a major player and does [b]THAT[/b] for them.

Borderlands 3 returns with the same solid Borderland experience of looting guns, gearing up, and having solid combat.  If you play it purely for the gameplay, you’ll still enjoy it here. 

However, the story just never clicks.  I’ve played for at least six hours with friends, and no character has resonated with me.  Beyond that, I hate the villains, not in a way I want them dead, but in a way, I just don’t care about them as villains, they’re stereotypes.  This is also a game that’s far better with friends, but there is a lot of content, interesting locations, and more. 

Pick this up if you like the Borderlands series, just don’t expect Handsome Jack or anything on the level of Borderland 2 or The Pre-Sequel’s writing.  I originally bought this game to play with buddies and I don’t mind picking it up to hang out with them, but I have no desire to play this on my own or finish the story, and that’s a pretty bad sign.   Still, it’s a fun game when my friends get together.

UPDATE: This game is unbearable due to unskippable dialogue. Apparently it's 3.5 HOURS of dialogue that you HAVE to listen to. 

However, there is a mod that cuts this all out. With that mod, the game is fun. I still do NOT recommend it, since I'm basing it on the vanilla game. 

I wouldn't recommend this at full price, or even anything over $30 (50%). 

PROS: The gameplay is fantastic. Multiplayer has been improved, the new vehicles, collectables, upgrades, classes, all are great. Whenever you're actively engaged in combat, the game is a lot of fun. 

CONS: So much of your time, in game, will be waiting to actually play. The devs have put so many unnecessary traffic lights in the path of progress. Most of the time, the game forces you to stop playing, put the controller down (or mouse/keys) and listen to their 'comedic riffs'. 

There are countless mission objectives that fall into four categories, which all break down to "stop playing and wait for us to tell you when to start again", and those are - 

1. WAIT FOR NPC: Yes, this is real. Your objective is to let time pass. That is absolutely disrespectful of the player's time. 
2. TALK TO NPC: Often you'll be waiting for an NPC to finish their 'super funny comedic monologue', so you'll go get some food, a drink, whatever...expecting to come back and have the game ready to let you play. But no, instead, you'll have a mission objective to CONTINUE the monologue. This feels like Gearbox's way of making sure you don't leave the computer while they're showing you how funny and clever they are. 
3. FOLLOW NPC: The problem with this is, again, that the NPCs don't start moving on their own, they will monologue, then the mission objective will go from "talking" to them, to "following" them, and that's usually because Gearbox wrote in too much to be said as they're walking. So the NPC has to tell their jokes, then you click them so they'll move, then they start telling more jokes as they're running. 
4: NO OBJECTIVE GIVEN: This happens all the time when you complete a mission. The screen just shows the checkmark, indicating the mission is done, but you have to stand around and wait for, you guessed it, more 'comedic monologues' as the NPCS joke about farts. Once their jokes are done, only THEN will your next mission pop up. 

EXAMPLE: The first egregious incident is on a mission where you have to rescue an NPC named Vaughn. This is one of your very first story missions. You find him, and he's hanging upside-down on a chain. The mission objective goes from "Find Vaughn" to "Shoot him down" (or something like that.)

Ok, so you shoot him down. He then starts his 'comedic riffing', and your mission objective is still 'shoot him down', but it's checked. He goes on for about 90 seconds, which doesn't seem like much, but again, you're not actually playing the game, you're just listening to Gearbox's jokes. 

After 90 seconds he says 'let's go!', and you'd think he'd start running, but he doesn't. He stands and waits for you to interact with him again, just to start him heading back towards safety. If you, knowing the fastest way back, get too far ahead of him, he will stop running and wait for you. When you both make it back to another NPC, you guessed it, more jokes and riffing before they tell you the next step. 

The game, for all its great mechanics, consistently forces the players to stop and wait. 

I put this as the huge con because the story and writing are awful, and it's exacerbated by the players being forced to stop playing the game, and listen. 

Then there's the fact that your character is completely inconsequential in the many, many cutscenes. Like, you'll watch the villains monologue for 5 minutes, saying they're going to kill someone, all right in front of you, then they kill that person, then Gearbox stops the cutscene and you can play again, having been made a total failure, with controls wrested away from you. 

Gearbox gave us a game that is really fun to play, then spends so much time taking the control away from us. 

I don't know how people do multiple playthroughs on this. I will say, I saw an improvement in Wonderlands, regarding the 'forced to listen' parts, but it's still there.
